rows: Most scorpions have one pair of median eyes on top of the head and several pairs of smaller lateral eyes at the front corners. The buthid scorpions that were checked all have five pairs of lateral eyes.
Scorpions are reported to see through a full 360 degrees around the body. The two median eyes overlap by about 40 degrees above the animal.

The eyes of two scorpion genera respond most to blue (470 nm) and green (525 nm) light, and scorpion eyes are often described as most sensitive to green. This view shows the world in shades of a single green-sensitive channel.
Scorpions are nocturnal, and their eyes are sensitive to starlight levels of light. In one species the median eyes are about 1000 times more sensitive at night than by day.
The median eyes are the main eyes and give relatively high acuity and good spatial discrimination. The lateral eyes may only detect changes in light.

No one has measured how much detail a scorpion sees. This view assumes a soft picture and lifts the brightness a little for night. The choice of colour channel, and the way the circle is squeezed into the screen, are the app's.
Sand scorpions sense insects moving up to about 50 cm away through vibrations in the ground, and hairs on the pedipalps sense wind direction. The camera records neither.
